before_outputs: frozen before E12 training; no model has been run on these words
amendments: before freezing and before any output: name filter extended to -ize/-ise forms and to plurals of a listed word (anglicize, americanize, cajuns, eurodollars appeared as 'names'); 'dink' excluded as a slur; the set was redrawn with the same seed

sampling.sources: SCOWL lower-case words (ordinary, irregular) and SCOWL capitalised entries not also lower-case (names), each with exactly one CMUdict reading (after stress removal)
sampling.ordinary: ≥ 2 Latin-token hits in the local FineWeb-2 Khmer shard and not irregular
sampling.names: capitalised SCOWL entries, minus derived forms ending in ['ian', 'ism', 'ist', 'ese', 'ic', 'ish', 'ite', 'ology', 'ize', 'ise', 'ized', 'izes', 'izing']
sampling.one_per_family: family_keys (reference_data.stems plus stripped suffixes), shared across all categories

exclusions: E03 dev/eval, E02 held-out sets, benchmark panels and the reserve (Latin inputs only, via e08.protected; no reserve target or E02 final reference is opened)
every historical Latin token in the repository (e06.historical_universe)
every arm R word (optimisation and train-val) and every E08 synthetic input
E10 confirmation words and the E10 and E11 review words (and their families)

e10_confirmation_audit.usage: E10 used its outputs only for operational diagnostics and an agreement rate; no recipe, data or decoding choice depended on them
e10_confirmation_audit.why_not_reused: unbalanced lengths (6 of 120 words ≤ 4 letters, 61 ≥ 9) and derived forms among the names (ethiopian, sikhism, brazilian)

scope: a single-judge test for this declared sample and docs/PHONETIC_POLICY.md, not a universal English→Khmer benchmark
